paper.title: Formalizing Learning from Language Feedback with Provable Guarantees

unmapped: Rewards are latent (never observed); the agent observes only stochastic (language) feedback O_t ~ f*(A_t) whose feedback mapping eta -> f_eta is unknown
Deterministic reward r*: A -> [0,1] parameterized by a hypothesis eta* in a known hypothesis space H; the learner knows the reward mapping eta -> r_eta (Assumption 1)
The learner has access to a hypothesis verifier loss l: A x O x H -> [0,1] (Assumption 2)
Unbiased feedback: each hypothesis minimizes the expected verifier loss under its own feedback distribution (Assumption 3)
settings.definition_quote: At time step $t$, the agent interacts with the environment by executing an action $A_t \in \actions$ and observing feedback $O_t \in \OO$ sampled from a feedback distribution $f^*:\actions \to \Delta(\OO)$; a reward $R_t = r^*(A_t)$ is incurred, based on a reward function $r^*:\actions\to[0,1]$, though $R_t$ is {\it not} revealed to the agent.

settings.name_in_paper: LLF with squared verifier loss (reward = E[g(a,o)])
unmapped: Rewards are latent; agent observes feedback O_t ~ f*(A_t)
r_eta(a) = E_{o~f_eta(a)}[g(a,o)] for a known g: A x O -> [0,1]; the learner knows g
Verifier loss is the squared loss l(a,o,eta) = (g(a,o) - r_eta(a))^2
Learner knows the reward mapping eta -> r_eta over a hypothesis space H
settings.definition_quote: Suppose $r_\eta(a) = \E_{o\sim f_\eta(a)} [g(a,o)]$ for some known $g:\actions\times\observations \to [0,1]$ and $\ell(a,o,\eta) = (g(a,o) - r_\eta(a))^2$ ... Suppose for all $t$, $g(A_t,O_t) - \E_{O'\sim f_\eta(A_t)}[g(A_t,O')]$ conditioned on $(\GG_t, A_t)$ is $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian.

algorithms.name: HELiX (Hypothesis Elimination using Language-informed Exploration; also called LLF-UCB)

symbols.N_cov: epsilon_T^H-covering number N(H, eps_T^H, d_H) of the hypothesis space under the verifier pseudometric d_H
symbols.dim_TE: epsilon_T^H-transfer eluder dimension dim_TE(H, l, eps_T^H)
symbols.eps_TH: max{1/T^2, min_a inf{|r_eta(a) - r*(a)| : eta != eta*}}

conditions: Assumption 1: agent knows the reward mapping eta -> r_eta
Assumption 2: hypothesis verifier loss l in [0,1] available
tuning: confidence sets with beta_t = sqrt(2t log(10 N t^2/(3 delta))) + 2 alpha t, delta = 1/T

source.label: thm:regret
source.quote: Under Assumptions \ref{as:reward mapping}--\ref{assum:unbiased-feedback}, for all $T\in\mathbb{N}$, ${\mathrm{Regret}}(T)$ of \algo is bounded by \widetilde{O} \left(  T^{3/4} \Big(\log N(\HH,\epsilon_T^\HH,d_\HH)\right)^{1/4}  \sqrt{ \dim_{TE} (\HH,\ell,\epsilon_T^\HH) } \Big)

results.notes: Regret defined via E[R_t] with deterministic rewards, so pseudo-regret. The algorithm takes T as input.

symbols.N_cov: covering number N(H, alpha, d_H) with alpha = eps_T^H

results.notes: The proof's last step uses eps_T^H <= 1/T^2, but eps_T^H is defined as a max with 1/T^2, so the inequality points the wrong way. The covering scale is written alpha in the statement and set to eps_T^H in the text.

symbols.beta_T: confidence-set width parameter of the version space at time T

conditions: with probability at least 1-delta, eta* in V_t for all t (for some delta in (0,1))
tuning: version spaces V_t = {eta : L_t(eta) <= min L_t + beta_t}

source.label: thm:abstract_regret
source.quote: If it holds that for some $\delta\in(0,1)$, with probability at least $1-\delta$, $\eta^*\in\VV_t$ for all $t$, then for all $T\in\mathbb{N}$, {\mathrm{Regret}}(T) \le 1 + \frac{1}{T} + \min\{\dim_{TE}(\HH,\ell,\epsilon_T^\HH), T\} + 2\sqrt{3\dim_{TE}(\HH,\ell,\epsilon_T^\HH)\beta_T T}.

results.notes: An abstract bound that holds only if the version spaces contain eta* with high probability. It is stated in terms of the algorithm's confidence parameter beta_T.

symbols.N_cov: epsilon_T^H-covering number of H under d_H

conditions: r_eta(a) = E_{o~f_eta(a)}[g(a,o)] for known g: A x O -> [0,1]

source.label: thm:fast_rate
source.quote: Suppose $r_\eta(a) = \E_{o\sim f_\eta(a)} [g(a,o)]$ for some known $g$ and $\ell(a,o,\eta) = (g(a,o) - r_\eta(a))^2$. Suppose ... is $\sigma$-sub-Gaussian. For all $T\in\mathbb{N}$, the regret of LLF-UCB satisfies {\mathrm{Regret}}(T) \le \widetilde{O}\left( \sqrt{ T \log N(\HH,\epsilon_T^\HH,d_\HH) \dim_{TE}(\HH,\ell,\epsilon_T^\HH) } \right)

results.notes: LLF-UCB is taken to be HELiX. No proof is given in the source.
